SMTO-LLM-0051 — The AI model sent an action SMTO couldn't identify

GUID: a64de902-d616-48a8-b099-7aa03dfabc60
Slug: model-tool-call-invalid
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • One of the actions in the model's reply was badly formed, for example missing its label or reusing another action's label. SMTO ran none of the actions in that reply.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the steps already shown for this task in the conversation and note which ones finished before the error. Work finished before this reply still stands, so you only need SMTO to continue, not redo it.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and pick a different model for Main (and Helper, if one is set), then save. Badly formed actions usually come from how a particular model or server writes them; another model often avoids it.
  3. If someone else runs your AI model server, ask them to check its tool-calling setup matches the model you use. A mismatched tool-calling setting on the server is a common reason actions arrive broken.
  4. Send a new message asking SMTO to continue from where it stopped, without repeating the steps that already finished. SMTO will only run actions it can identify clearly, so a clean reply lets the task continue.

What success looks like

  • SMTO carries out the model's next action and the task continues without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your AI model server. Don't ask SMTO to redo steps that already finished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A tool_calls entry is not an object, has a type other than 'function', or has an empty or duplicate call id, so the turn was rejected before dispatch.

What this means

  • A tool-call member has an invalid record type, function type or identity; the full turn must establish valid distinct calls before admission. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • A tool-call member has an invalid record type, function type or identity; the full turn must establish valid distinct calls before admission.

How to diagnose it

  • Check call object shape, function type and unique nonempty call identities at the strict boundary.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the raw tool_calls from the configured endpoint: each entry needs type 'function', a unique nonempty id and a function object. Fix the server's tool parser (for vLLM, the --tool-call-parser that matches this model) or route to a compatible endpoint in Settings › Setup › Model routing.
  • Check the endpoint’s tool parser and advertised native call schema. Correct the malformed representation before another operation is authorized.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Every call record validates and has an unambiguous identity before dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
